text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's private telecommunication company Mobicom said it would pay 1.2 billion levs dividends for last year to its shareholders.
-- Bulgaria's state Hebros bank has acquired a 67.5 percent stake in the state cannery Domat against unpaid debts worth 188 million levs, Agriculture ministry said.

-- Depositors in Bulgaria's private Mollovbank, which was placed in receivership last year, should be able to recover their deposits after the Slovak investment fund Istrocapital bought a 92 percent stake in the bank, board chairman Assen Hristov said.
-- Bulgaria is not expected to raise electricity prices until the autumn, deputy prime minister Alexander Bozhkov said.
-- The Bulgarian National Bank foreign currency reserves rose by $100 million in March from $445.5 in February, Finance minister Svetoslav Gavriiski said.

-- Bulgaria's Gross Domestic Product is expected to fall by six percent this year and annual inflation is expected at 2,000 percent, a forecast by the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development said.
-- The Sofia City court is expected to rule on an insolvency suit against the private Elitbank filed by the Bulgarian National Bank on June 26, court officials said.
-- The private Bulgarian-Russian Investment bank said its paid-in capital totalled 2.440 billion levs.
-- Bulgaria's private Trade and Industry Bank said it had posted 1.2 billion levs pre-tax profit for last year.
-- Bulgaria exported more than 200 million litres of wine worth some $40 million last year, the Union of wine makers said.

-- The Sofia City Court postponed a ruling on an insolvency case against the Bank for Agricultural Credit filed by the Bulgarian National Bank to May 15, private Balkan news agency said quoting court officials. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
